title: Kushner Meets Sisi and Hamas Chief Al-Hayya in El-Alamein to Press Disarmament Roadmap
detail: US envoy Jared Kushner met Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi in El-Alamein on August 16, 2026 to discuss ceasefire implementation, then held talks with Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya alongside Board of Peace representatives Nickolay Mladenov and Tony Blair, plus Egyptian, Qatari, and Turkish officials. Kushner pushed Hamas to begin disarming despite Prime Minister Netanyahu's public rejection of the 15-point roadmap, and urged the group to halt public displays of armed fighters and hand administrative authority to the Palestinian National Committee for Gaza Administration (NCAG). Hamas indicated it would only proceed with disarmament if Israel first upheld its own ceasefire commitments. A Board of Peace source said the first weapons handover to the NCAG is unlikely before year-end, as the planned International Stabilization Force remains in early training. Separately, Egypt, Jordan, the UAE, Qatar, Turkey, Pakistan, and Indonesia issued a joint statement blaming Israel for 'disrupting peace efforts in Gaza' and calling on the Board of Peace to enforce Israeli compliance with the plan.

media.caption: Kushner meets Sisi and Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya in El-Alamein, Egypt, to press the stalled Gaza disarmament roadmap

title: IDF Strikes Target PIJ Operative in Khan Younis, Hamas Operative in Nuseirat
detail: The IDF carried out two separate strikes in Gaza on August 16, 2026: one targeting a Palestinian Islamic Jihad operative in Khan Younis, and another targeting a Hamas operative in Nuseirat. The military described both as 'precise aerial strikes' against operatives it said were 'advancing attacks' against Israeli forces or civilians, framed as permitted under the ceasefire's self-defense provisions.

media.caption: IDF strikes target a Palestinian Islamic Jihad operative in Khan Younis and a Hamas operative in Nuseirat

title: Israeli Drone Strike Hits Displacement Tent Near Al-Aqsa University in Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis
detail: An Israeli drone struck a tent sheltering displaced people near Al-Aqsa University in the Al-Mawasi area west of Khan Younis on August 16, 2026, killing at least one Palestinian and wounding several others, medical sources told Anadolu Agency. The strike was among several reported across Gaza that day, part of what rights monitors describe as a pattern of repeated Israeli strikes on displacement tents in the nominally 'safe' Al-Mawasi humanitarian zone.

media.caption: Israeli drone strike hits a displacement tent near Al-Aqsa University in Al-Mawasi, west of Khan Younis

title: 14-Year-Old Suhail Abu Shalouf Shot Dead While Collecting Firewood Near Yellow Line
detail: Suhail Masoud Abu Shalouf, 14, was shot and killed by Israeli forces on the evening of August 16, 2026 while gathering firewood in the Al-Mawasi area south of Khan Younis, near the Yellow Line. The Palestinian Red Crescent Society recovered his body; his family said his brother had previously been killed by Israeli forces. Separately the same day, a child was shot and injured by an Israeli quadcopter drone east of the Bureij refugee camp, and several Palestinians were wounded when a strike hit the roof of a house in the Nuseirat refugee camp. Gaza's Health Ministry said 1,262 Palestinians have been killed and 4,168 wounded since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect.

media.caption: 14-year-old Suhail Abu Shalouf shot dead while collecting firewood near the Yellow Line south of Khan Younis

title: Ben Gvir Advocates Killing '30 to 40' Palestinians in Gaza Nightly on Ex-Hostage's Podcast
detail: National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir said in a taped interview on former hostage Rom Braslavski's podcast, which surfaced August 16, 2026, that Israel should conduct 'targeted assassinations' in Gaza, 'taking down 30 to 40 every night,' criticizing Netanyahu's recent scaling back of strikes. Ben Gvir argued Israel should not limit itself to killing 'those who endanger us in that moment,' saying of some Palestinians that 'they aren't worthy of life; they shouldn't be alive; they aren't people at all.' He also renewed calls for Palestinian emigration from Gaza and new Israeli settlement of the territory. Ben Gvir holds no direct military authority but sits on Israel's security cabinet.

media.caption: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir calls for killing '30 to 40' Palestinians in Gaza nightly
